ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an AND-function module with a tri-state output stage, with an “&” mark inside the box; there are two data inputs on the left side, both labeled 1; there is an enable terminal EN on the lower left side, whose input is labeled 0; the output terminal on the right side is labeled F, and has a tri-state output/output driver symbol. Reasoning: This circuit can be regarded as an AND-function tri-state output stage. Although the ordinary AND gate result of the two data inputs 1 AND 1 would be 1, the tri-state output first depends on the enable terminal. In the figure EN=0, indicating that the enable is not asserted, so the output driver is disabled and does not drive F according to the ordinary AND gate result. When the driver is off, F is in a high-impedance state.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual circuit: identify the block as an AND-function tri-state output stage, note the two data inputs are 1 and 1, and note the enable pin EN is 0. Then apply the tri-state rule: since EN is not asserted, do not evaluate F as the normal AND output; instead the output driver is disabled. Conclude that F is in the high-impedance state.
